gilbert goudie and jón a. hjaltalín.bio:
Gilbert Goudie (1843–1918) and Jón A. Hjaltalín (1840–1908) were pioneering scholars whose collaborative efforts were instrumental in bringing the rich heritage of Old Norse literature to an English-speaking audience. Goudie, a distinguished Scottish antiquary and authority on the history of the Northern Isles, combined his deep archival expertise with Hjaltalín’s profound linguistic mastery as an Icelandic scholar and librarian. Together, they bridged the cultural divide between the Viking Age and the modern era, meticulously documenting the historical and geographical connections between Scotland and the North Atlantic world.

Their definitive translation of The Orkneyinga Saga remains a cornerstone of medieval scholarship, celebrated for its precision and its evocative rendering of the saga’s epic narrative. By grounding their work in a rigorous understanding of the landscapes—from the treacherous waters of the Minch to the rugged shores of the Hebrides—they provided readers with an essential key to unlocking the complex genealogies and power struggles of the Norse earls. This enduring contribution continues to serve as a vital resource for historians and literary enthusiasts alike, preserving the legacy of the Northmen with scholarly integrity and narrative grace.
